_what_this_is: Resolution of the five candidates raised by the executed search. Written as a SEPARATE record and not as an amendment to SEARCH-RECORD.json, because that file is anchored: editing it would break the published hash and its worked example. The search record states what the search returned; this states what screening made of it.
method: Each candidate's REGISTERED PRIMARY OUTCOME MEASURE was read from the ClinicalTrials.gov outcome module via mcp__plugin_bio-research_c-trials__analyze_endpoints. The search record's provisional axes were read from registry TITLES; a title is not an outcome definition, and one of the five turned out to differ from its title-based axis.
review_estimand: First occurrence of adjudicated cardiovascular death or adjudicated hospitalisation for heart failure, as a time-to-first-event hazard ratio, in adults with heart failure.

resolutions.registered_primary: Percentage of Pairwise Comparisons With Wins of Clinical Benefit -- a hierarchical composite of death, number of HF events, time to first HF event, and >=5-point change in KCCQ-TSS at 90 days
resolutions.reason: A win ratio over a hierarchical composite is not a time-to-first-event hazard ratio. Excluded on the measure axis, not on quality.
resolutions.NOT_A_SILENT_EXCLUSION: EMPULSE DOES report this review's outcome concept -- 'Incidence Rate of First Occurrence of Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Heart Failure Event' -- but as a SECONDARY endpoint and as an incidence rate per 100 patient-years, not as a hazard ratio. Recorded so a reader can see the trial was assessed rather than overlooked, and so the exclusion is not mistaken for the trial ignoring the outcome.

resolutions.registered_primary: Change from baseline to week 12 in 6-minute walk test distance
resolutions.reason: Exercise capacity, not a clinical event composite. No cardiovascular-death or heart-failure-hospitalisation endpoint appears at primary OR secondary level.

resolutions.registered_primary: Change from baseline to week 12 in 6-minute walk test distance
resolutions.reason: Exercise capacity, not a clinical event composite. No cardiovascular-death or heart-failure-hospitalisation endpoint appears at primary OR secondary level.

resolutions.registered_primary: Composite of Time to First Heart Failure Hospitalisation or ALL-CAUSE Mortality, reported as an incidence rate per 100 patient-years
resolutions.THE_TITLE_BASED_AXIS_WAS_INCOMPLETE: The search record recorded this as a population exclusion alone, read from the title. The outcome module shows a SECOND difference the title does not reveal: the composite is heart-failure hospitalisation or ALL-CAUSE mortality, whereas this review's composite is CARDIOVASCULAR death or heart-failure hospitalisation. Those are different composites. This is the concrete instance of why a title is not an outcome definition, and it is recorded rather than quietly upgraded.
resolutions.reason: Population is patients with acute myocardial infarction, not adults with heart failure; and the registered composite uses all-cause mortality rather than cardiovascular death. Either alone would exclude it.

resolutions.registered_primary: Change from baseline to week 12 in PCr/ATP ratio at rest, by 31P cardiac magnetic resonance spectroscopy
resolutions.reason: A cardiac energetics biomarker. The trial registers NO secondary endpoints at all, so no clinical event outcome exists on this record.

outcome.STATEMENT: The registry search returned seven phase-3 empagliflozin-versus-placebo trials. Five differ from this review's estimand on population or measure, each on a stated axis read from the registered outcome module rather than from a title. The two the review already held are the two that report the registered estimand. On these sources, the included set is not a convenience sample: it is a set that has now been searched for and cannot be improved on.

WHAT_THIS_DOES_NOT_ESTABLISH: NOT that the included set is complete. 676 of 776 PubMed records were never retrieved, and a trial reported only in the literature and not registered on ClinicalTrials.gov would not appear in the registry limb at all.
NOT an adequate search. Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science and Scopus were not searched.
NOT a full-text screen. These are registry-record decisions; none of the five was excluded after reading its publication.
NOT independent screening. One screener, one pass. The protocol requires two cross-family screeners for a release, and that has not happened here.
